lesson.title: 911-Procedure 103 – CALL ANSWERING PROCEDURE
lesson.topic: NYPD Calltaking – Call Flow & Operator Rules
objectives: Apply the official required NYC 911 greeting verbatim.
Verify caller location using cross streets and apartment/floor info.
Follow the correct call flow: greeting → location → callback → emergency.
Use professional calltaker language and avoid prohibited phrasing.
End every call with the required identification statement including operator number.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the REQUIRED NYC 911 greeting that must be stated verbatim?

choices.text: Emergency services, what do you need?
New York City 911, do you need Police, Fire or Medical?
911, what's going on?
NYPD, please state your emergency.

questions.solution: The procedure requires this exact greeting at the start of every call.

questions.stem: According to the procedure, what is the correct order for the initial steps of the call?

choices.text: Emergency → greeting → location → callback
Greeting → location → callback → emergency
Callback → emergency → greeting → location
Location → greeting → callback → emergency

questions.solution: The training specifies greeting first, then verifying location, then callback, then emergency.

questions.stem: Why must the calltaker always ask the caller for the two streets the address is between?

choices.text: It makes the caller feel more comfortable.
It verifies the location in the system and ensures responders are sent to the correct place.
It is only necessary for fire emergencies.
It's optional unless the caller sounds unsure.

questions.solution: Cross streets are required to verify the exact location and ensure accurate response routing.

questions.stem: Which option contains language that is PROHIBITED according to the call-answering procedure?

choices.text: Sir, I need you to speak slowly please.
Ma’am, I am trying to understand you.
You need to calm down or I can’t help you.
Thank you, I understand.

questions.solution: The procedure forbids escalating language and anything that blames the caller.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST aligns with the procedure’s requirement for obtaining building details?

choices.text: Apartment and floor information are optional if the caller sounds stressed.
Apartment/floor info must be included with the address whenever applicable.
Calltakers should only ask for apartment numbers on burglary calls.
Address is enough; apartment/floor info is added by dispatch.

questions.solution: The procedure requires collecting apartment and floor details as part of proper address entry.

questions.stem: The required NYC 911 greeting must be spoken exactly as written in the procedure.
It is acceptable to threaten to disconnect the caller if they are yelling or upset.
Cross streets must always be asked for when verifying an address, regardless of the type of emergency.
Calltakers are required to give their operator number only when the caller requests it.
The correct order of the call flow begins with greeting, then verifying the caller’s __________.
At the end of a call, the required statement includes: “Assistance will be provided as soon as possible, Operator #_____.”
Match each step of the call with its correct purpose.
answer: Start the call with the mandated phrase
Confirm where the emergency is happening
Ensure we can reach the caller if disconnected

questions.stem: Match each phrase to whether it is PERMITTED or PROHIBITED.
answer: “Stop yelling or I can’t help you.”
“Calm down or I will disconnect the call.”

questions.stem: Why does the procedure require the greeting to be spoken the same way every time?

choices.text: To let calltakers improvise the opening.
To maintain consistency and meet legal/procedural standards.
To make the greeting shorter.
So callers know which operator they reached.

questions.solution: Standardized greeting ensures uniformity, clarity, and compliance with official policy.

questions.stem: Why does the procedure place LOCATION so early in the call flow?

choices.text: Because location is optional, but it's easy to ask first.
So units can be sent quickly even if the call disconnects.
To avoid having to ask for the caller’s name.
So the caller feels more comfortable.

questions.solution: Location is needed to dispatch help; getting it early protects against disconnects.

questions.stem: According to the call-answering procedure, what is the main reason for confirming a callback number?

choices.text: To sign the caller up for alerts.
So the calltaker can call back if the line disconnects.
To verify the caller's identity for billing.
It is not required in emergencies.

questions.solution: Callback confirmation ensures contact if the call drops or more information is needed.

questions.stem: The procedure emphasizes staying calm and professional. What is the BEST example of procedure-compliant caller control?

choices.text: “If you don't stop yelling, I’m going to hang up.”
“I need you to take a breath so I can understand and get you help.”
“If you keep talking like that, I won’t help you.”
“I’m tired of repeating myself, listen carefully.”

questions.solution: The procedure supports calm, directive language that focuses on understanding and getting help.

questions.stem: The procedure requires asking, “What two streets are you between?” primarily to:

choices.text: Check if the caller knows the neighborhood.
Verify the address and improve dispatch accuracy.
Delay the call while preparing the screen.
Determine which operator will handle the case.

questions.solution: Cross streets help confirm the location so responders go to the correct place.

questions.stem: Which prompt BEST matches the procedure for obtaining apartment or floor information?

choices.text: “If you want, you can tell me the floor, but it’s not important.”
“What is the apartment or floor number where this is happening?”
“I’ll let the officers figure out which floor it is.”
“Is this close to the lobby or not really?”

questions.solution: Apartment/floor details must be explicitly captured when applicable, not left for responders to guess.

questions.stem: Which closing line BEST follows the procedure for ending a call?

choices.text: “Okay, good luck. Try to stay safe.”
“Assistance will be provided as soon as possible, Operator #____.”
“If you have more problems, call back later.”
“That’s all I can do, goodbye.”

questions.solution: The procedure requires the specific closing phrase including the operator number.

questions.stem: The procedure requires greeting, then location, then callback, then emergency.
It is acceptable to replace the official greeting with your own version as long as the caller understands you.
According to the procedure, calltakers must avoid blaming language, even if the caller is yelling or upset.
The required end-of-call statement includes the operator number on every call, not only when the caller requests it.
Match each step of the call-answering procedure with what the calltaker focuses on at that step.
answer: State the official phrase that opens every call
Get address, cross streets, and apartment/floor details
Confirm the best number to reach the caller
Find out what is happening and what help is needed

questions.stem: Match the phrase with whether it is consistent with the procedure.
answer: “Ma’am, I need you to speak slowly so I can help you.”
“If you keep yelling, I’m going to hang up on you.”
“If you don’t calm down, I won’t send anyone.”

questions.stem: The required greeting begins: “New York City __________, do you need Police, Fire or Medical?”
To confirm the location, calltakers are required to ask: “What two __________ are you between?”
The procedure teaches the call flow as: greeting, location, callback, and then the caller’s __________.
At the end of the call, the calltaker must say: “Assistance will be provided as soon as possible, __________ #_____.”
